page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.2xlarge is a storage-oriented virtual instance belonging to the Local SSDs family. Built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Supporting hardware acceleration includes AVX-512 vector and VNNI extensions. It integrates 32 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per vCPU distribution, alongside 479 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage and a 3 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluations reveal steady mid-tier capability across general computing workloads. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 4479.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 8286.39, while software compilation via Clang reaches 6737.0. Memory bandwidth delivers 50.63 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 38.88 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the instance yields 6.88 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 6.92 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Tradeoffs are evident in single-threaded bottlenecks; stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression rank in the lower quartile, and prompt processing for 7B parameter language models registers in the bottom decile at 10.56 tokens per second.

By incorporating 479 GB of local SSD capacity alongside a 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration, the instance delivers a practical resource profile without requiring separate external block storage for high-frequency operations. It is best deployed for I/O-sensitive transactional workloads, including relational databases, Redis caching layers, web serving infrastructure, and general enterprise microservices that rely on low-latency local disk access.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3g.2xlarge is a local SSD instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs from a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor, 32 GB of RAM, and 479 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage. Designed with a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration delivers balanced compute and memory capacity alongside low-latency local storage. Benchmark results show midrange performance across general compute suites, scoring 4479.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 8286.39 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory subsystems demonstrate stable throughput, with uncached large-block reads achieving 50.63 GB/sec and Redis SET performance reaching 6.88 million operations per second. However, single-core processing and compression tasks show lower relative throughput, and heavy LLM inference exhibits poor scaling. With integrated local SSD capacity and a 3 Gbps baseline network interface, this instance offers practical operational efficiency for transactional databases, web serving tiers, caching layers, and data-intensive enterprise workloads requiring fast local disk access.
